name: Northern Yukaghir
notes: Northern (Tundra) Yukaghir, Yukaghir family (an isolate-level branch outside Uralic), Sakha Republic/Chukotka, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: Tundra Yukaghir Cyrillic orthography, NFC. ⟨ӷ⟩/⟨ӻ⟩ (two attested spellings across sources for the same uvular fricative letter) map to /ʁ/, and ⟨ӄ⟩ maps to the uvular stop /q/ (Maslova 2003 Tundra Yukaghir; NorthEuraLex йоӻул -> j o ʁ u l). ⟨л⟩ is the plain lateral /l/ and ⟨ль⟩ is its palatalised counterpart /lʲ/, the ordinary Cyrillic hard/soft-consonant convention: an earlier revision of this spec had the contrast reversed (⟨л⟩ velarised default /lˠ/, ⟨ль⟩ plain /l/) under the DOI/title pairing corrected in the maslova2003tundra source note; Schmalz's consonant table (2013, Table 2.1.2, printed p.30) lists only a plain-vs-palatalised /l/~/l'/ contrast with no velarised member, and NorthEuraLex's own Segments column agrees, transcribing л as plain [l] (хуруул -> xuruːl) and ль as palatalised [lʲ] (хайль -> xajlʲ) with no counterexample found in the wired gold. Vowel length is spelled by doubling the vowel letter (⟨аа⟩ /a̟ː/, ⟨оо⟩ /o̞ː/, ⟨уу⟩ /uː/, ⟨ии⟩ /ɪː/) — a real length contrast, not free repetition, so the doubled forms are separate keys (Maslova 2003 Tundra Yukaghir). ⟨и⟩ and ⟨е⟩/⟨э⟩ map to the lax /ɪ/ and /ɛ/ phonemes of this inventory (already declared in this spec's ``allophones``, which give [i] and [e] as their open surface variants) rather than to tense /i/ /e/, matching the cited PHOIBLE inventory. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨ч⟩ maps to the affricate /tʃ/ and the palatalised coronals ⟨нь⟩/⟨дь⟩ to /nʲ/ /dʲ/, Maslova's own transcription convention for Tundra Yukaghir, preferred over this spec's inherited PHOIBLE symbols /c/ /ɲ/ /ɟ/ (a different source's narrower phonetic notation for the same segments); NorthEuraLex evidence (чилгэ 'tʃilge', ньилла 'nʲilla', өдьил 'ødʲil') corroborates the affricate/palatalised-coronal reading. Word stress in Tundra Yukaghir is lexical but is not consistently orthographically marked in the practical Cyrillic script; documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog. NorthEuraLex's Segments column is a broad/simplified IPA transcription that drops the narrow phonetic diacritics this spec's grapheme table carries (advanced [a̟] surfaces in gold as plain [a], lowered [o̞] as plain [o], lax [ɪ]/[ɛ] as tense [i]/[e]); this is the same dataset-wide NorthEuraLex convention already documented in this repo's ale/ain/bsk/enf/mhr/sel/sia/sms/yrk specs, not a defect specific to this row, and it accounts for most of the row's remaining PER after the lateral fix.

sources.notes: Grammar sketch of Tundra (Northern) Yukaghir: Cyrillic orthography, ⟨ӷ⟩/⟨ӻ⟩ /ʁ/, ⟨ӄ⟩ /q/, vowel-length spelling by letter doubling, and the lexical-but-unmarked status of stress. This spec previously cited this author/year under DOI 10.1515/9783110197174, which resolves (verified against De Gruyter's own listing) to Maslova's separate Mouton Grammar Library monograph 'A Grammar of Kolyma Yukaghir' — Southern Yukaghir, iso639_3 yux, a different book about a different language; that DOI/title pairing is removed, and no section/page locator is carried over from it because none was verified against this book's actual text.

sources.notes: Table 2.1.2, consonant inventory (printed p.30): the lateral series is plain /l/ vs palatalised /l'/, with no velarised member; the following remarks (p.30-31) note /l/ can be hard to distinguish from /l'/ before /e/. NorthEuraLex's own Segments column agrees: л is transcribed plain [l] (e.g. хуруул -> xuruːl) and ль palatalised [lʲ] (e.g. хайль -> xajlʲ).
